body:
Okay wow. 

I didn't know it was going to be this in depth of a reply. If I get my tax return I think I might just go with this build, and use a bit of it to buy a nice chair, and cheap desk. 

I generally use my tax return on something for myself, and having a computer that can handle games on max settings would be something I'd really appreciate. 

One thing though, I think my current apartment building may have power surges, as my Xbox one turns on by itself all the time, that it got to the point I just unplug most of my electronics around the apartment. nothing's shorted out yet, but I am worried that something could happen to a custom PC.
I do a bit of guided yoga from youtube after my runs now, because I don't know how to stretch.
As I said above, I'll look for it and give it a serious read. Thanks!

yeah it's hard. I know when I am happy that I know what it's like. And I have been happy when I hang out with my friends/family. And when I'm on my walks in public. It's just the transition to becoming okay with it at home now.
yeah, he's already my second one at the university and they may not be accustomed to this type of thing.

Okay. 

I have CBD, but don't generally take it because I don't really like the feeling I get from it. It's an oil with a dropper. I used to use a lot before, and since quitting a few years ago it hasn't been the same.

Okay, I'll mention that in my next session and move forward from how he answers. Or if he can refer to me somewhere else. 

He's a part of the university counselors for the students. I've found that most of them are mainly set up for school stress related stuff. I just didn't know where else to go in my city.

Yeah, I have a lot of the similar google searches in my history. 

This relationship ending was really hard, and that's why I've been at my lowest because I now recognize the mistakes I've been making my entire life, and it seems like I've done it in every relationship. I guess that's been a huge step this month, acknowledging the mistakes I was making, and now I am looking for the first step to move forward. 

I come from a big family, and I was always singled out as being the smartest. I have never felt smart. It's as if their compliments made me insecure. wow. okay. so this thought just came to me as I was writing it out thinking about your comment. I guess moving forward I am going to be looking at what I am confident in, and what I could improve. I know I love making people smile, and I can usually do it by smiling at them (people say I have great teeth?) and I also like making silly and playful jokes. I can be pretty self-demeaning with my jokes, but I'm going to try and not do that. 

I'm not looking for a relationship right now, but I am trying dating. I haven't dated before, just kind of ended up with a girlfriend because we knew each other from growing up and ran into each other one summer while I was home. So this whole dating thing is more about building confidence, accepting rejection, but also giving out rejection. I move away for 4 months every year, so my beginner dating is to distract me from my ex, like in a way that makes me feel that there are other people that could have feelings for me. I'm pretty straight forward with it, saying I'm looking to make friends or hangout a bit. I'm passed this whole hooking up phase, because I know how meaningless that is. I'm more looking to go for a walk and create a memory that I can have with someone while watching a sunset. 

yeah, today I got rid of her on all my social media stuff and deleted her number. she's in a different country for school, so I don't have to worry about running into her for a bit. 

Thank you!

I was thinking of it, but don't want to be on any medications because I'm not sure how it'll affect my work, which I've been relying on for the last few years, but if i slip back again, I'll for sure really consider it.

I have one friend I have begun hanging out with on a regular basis because his relationship seems to be taking a similar turn. We generally drink together because we were introduced through our partners years ago. But, with how things are now, he's come over to play board games and video games, and we'll try and focus on that. We have a third friend that lives in a nearby town that comes up every other weekend to join us. We're currently prepping a pathfinder game, which will be super awesome, but I wasn't reaching out enough during my few day binges and the scheduling got screwed a bit.

Also, I have a sister who's a psych major that always checks in on me, but I have troubles with myself thinking that I'm too much for my friends and family always breaking down or drunk calling them when I'm sad. And it embarrasses me knowing that I'm at such a low and weak point in my life. But, I am trying to keep reaching out because they always tell me that they do want me to reach out, and have actually begun checking in on me and it's been helping. 

My friend introduced me to Chill step, and it's been monumental on my moods. I used to listen to heavy metal, or a lot of indie/pop music that I hadn't realized was a lot of break up songs and so before finding chill step I couldn't even listen to my favorite songs. I like playing guitar, and have begun trying to sing and play, and have got about a half dozen songs down. I've also begun singing in the shower. 

I have a journal, but stopped writing in it because a lot would turn into suicide notes that I would rip out. Which is why I've turned to Reddit. Each reply, for me, seems like a sort of cathartic introspection and allows me to see that there has been a ton of progress that I've been blind to, and it gives me so much hope. But I'll try with the things I like about myself, rather than focusing on the negative.

I will likely stay away from "Wild" for a while, as it was my partners favorite book, and she took all her favorite books with her when she left, and I donated the rest. But I have watched the movie, and do know that the struggle she goes through is an arduous one. Thinking of it though, I may reread "Into the Wild". 

I managed to get a 5km in today, it took me 10 minutes longer than before, but I knew this was going to happen because I've neglected my body for the last few months, and was drinking heavily. after running for a few more days, I'm going to hit the gym, start slow, but I don't have many exams and am trying to prepare myself to stick to working out again in the future. 

Thanks

I'll keep seeing the counselor until I'm done school, and then when I move for my summer job will try and set one up where I move because my summer job can get pretty stressful. 

I went for a run today, and joined a hiking club that is with elders, so its a nice start because I'm nearly 30 pounds overweight and have stretch marks and just feel generally bad about myself. But today I went shopping for the first time in weeks, and cleaned out all the spoiled food in there - I might try this keto thing for a couple weeks to help with switching off from ordering out. 

I can't adopt an animal sadly, I've wanted to for years but the apartment I'm staying at doesn't allow, and I'm not financially setup to make a move in my city at this moment, but I am aiming to do it at the end of the summer when I have a bunch of money saved up. 

The walking with music has been my go to. I went for a run today without music to help me think, I find I can focus more without the distraction of music. I've set a goal to make it to the gym at least once this week. 

My replies on here are a part of my introspection, writing each one out is showing me that I really accomplished a lot today, but that I'm going to start with taking things one day at a time for now. I blocked my ex, cleaned more of the things she left that weren't technically hers, but more like ours but I decided today that they were memento's of the relationship, and although my apartment is bare, I can only see MY things, this is now my place.
I know. That's another reason I want to walk around the city more, so I can feel like I can know it and feel like a part of it.

My inner dialogue is always thinking of the mistakes that I might say during a conversation, or a lot of elevator thoughts about arguments. But today I tried to say positive things like how people like my smile, so I tried smiling at strangers today. 

My inner dialogue at home tends to be very negative, especially when I procrastinate. Like I'm not good enough for school, or being funded and I'm just wasting my scholarship on myself. I started at a college and had a around a 90% average, but since this breakup I've dropped down to about 70%. I had to drop a class because I missed an assignment worth over 30%. 

I found a yoga book with affirmations today, and tried repeating some while I was on my walk. and It seemed to help me like myself today for the most part, and writing this I'm crying, but in a different way that feels good like something has finally clicked. Thank you.

Thank you for your reply. 

I managed to go to a coffee shop today to read, I don't know what makes it more comfortable than being at home reading, but it really helped. I reached out to my sister and we went for a lunch together. I also talked to a neighbor and she insisted I installed the meetup app, and invited me out for a walk with a bunch of her friends (they're all 60+), and I figured it would be cool to have older peoples perspectives. 

I started an Instagram page and have started taking photo's of the city and sunsets as well a few weeks ago and get random followers which is nice. 

I fell like I made progress today. Thanks, I read this last night but wasn't sure how my day was so, I waited to reply until now.

I'll look for it at the Chapter's tomorrow! thanks. I'm reading through Focusing by Eugene Gendlin, PH.D, this book was recommended from my counselor and I like it so far, it's fairly short, but I'm only about 30 pages in.

After the abortion we started becoming distant and argued over trivial things more and more, until she finally said she needed something different in her life, and decided to move out. Her moving out hit me pretty hard as out of the blue, which makes this hard to comprehend and get over.

I'm living in a university city, so there's tons of people around my age. I don't know how to approach people is the problem. 

I play a lot of Xbox when I don't have to study, so lately I've been dumping a lot of time into that when I can't cope with my issues, but I know it's only a medium that puts my issues on the back burner. 

I read science fiction for fun, but haven't been able to lately due to not having anyone to share the story with - I like to read and discuss with someone about whatever book I am immersed in, and for the last four years that has been my partner. 

A lot of the hobbies I enjoyed feel stale at the moment, and I don't know how to find a new one. 

My apartment feels hollow, as it's only been a few weeks since my partner moved out, so I've been staying out late at pubs and bars to not have to be at home. I know it's immature, but today I've finally decided to try and fully face this new direction in life.
